brief: Rule-based, long-only strategy on a fixed 10-ETF universe; trades on >= 3 days every week; weekly turnover <= 20%; daily closing prices only; maximise long-run growth with max drawdown < 20%, diversified.

criteria.name: legal_and_ethical
criteria.definition: No market manipulation, no non-public information, no prohibited practices.

criteria.name: long_only_fixed_universe
criteria.definition: Weights in the 10 listed ETFs are >= 0 and sum to <= 1; any remainder is uninvested cash. No leverage, shorting, derivatives or other instruments.

criteria.name: trades_three_days_per_week
criteria.definition: The rules produce trades on at least 3 trading days in every full week (holiday weeks: as many as trading days allow).

criteria.name: turnover_cap
criteria.definition: Weekly turnover, defined as the sum of absolute weight changes divided by 2 over each calendar week, is at most 20% by construction.

criteria.name: daily_close_data_only
criteria.definition: Signals use only daily closing prices and quantities derived from them (returns, volatility, correlations, moving averages); no intraday, fundamental or alternative data.

criteria.name: growth
criteria.definition: Plausible long-run compound growth after realistic trading costs.
anchors: strong: a clearly stated economic or statistical mechanism for return, with a reasoned net-of-cost estimate
weak: return relies on an effect likely consumed by costs, or no mechanism is given

criteria.name: drawdown_control
criteria.definition: How convincingly the rules keep maximum drawdown below 20%, including in correlated stress (2008, 2020, 2022).
anchors: strong: an explicit de-risking rule plus a reasoned worst-case estimate addressed to correlated sell-offs
middle: a risk rule without an argument for the 20% bound
weak: drawdown left to diversification alone

criteria.name: diversification
criteria.definition: Risk spread across asset classes at each point in time, not only on average.
anchors: strong: no single class dominates risk at any date, by rule
weak: effectively an equity-beta bet most of the time

criteria.name: robustness
criteria.definition: Few parameters chosen on stated principles; expected to work across regimes rather than fit one history.
anchors: strong: parameters justified ex ante, behaviour argued across regimes
weak: many tuned thresholds with no principle

criteria.name: constraint_fit
criteria.definition: How naturally the rules satisfy the trade-frequency and turnover constraints while still acting on the signal.
anchors: strong: a stated mechanism (e.g. staggered or tranched rebalancing) makes both constraints hold without crippling the signal
weak: constraints bolted on as clipping that fights the signal

criteria.name: specificity
criteria.definition: Rules precise and feasible enough that two people would code the same strategy from the stated data.
anchors: strong: every lookback, threshold, rebalance day, weight formula and tie-break is stated

criteria.name: novelty
criteria.definition: Adds something beyond textbook momentum or a static 60/40, or develops a known idea in a genuinely new way.
anchors: strong: a new mechanism or combination with a stated reason it should work

assumptions: Maximum drawdown below 20% is judged, not gated: critics cannot verify it without a backtest.
Trading costs are estimates: about 2-5 bp per trade for large liquid ETFs, up to about 10 bp for emerging-market, commodity and REIT ETFs.
Signals are computed on the close of day t and traded at the close of day t+1.
Web research is off for this demo; agents rely on their own knowledge.
Judged criteria are compared pairwise, not scored on scales, so no weights are set.
